original_question: Characterize the well-filtered dcpos, meaning the directed complete partial orders that admit some well-filtered topology compatible with their original order.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's target as Question 4.3 in Section 4, and it already captures the intended meaning from Definition 4.1: the problem is to characterize those dcpos that admit some well-filtered topology compatible with their given order. It also correctly avoids drifting into the different notion of a Scott well-filtered dcpo.
missing_details: The paper's notion of compatibility should be stated explicitly: a topology τ on P is compatible with the original order iff cl_τ({x}) = ↓x for every x in P (Section 4, immediately before Definition 4.1, page 5).
The topology sought is a T0 well-filtered topology on the underlying set of P, since well-filtered spaces are T0 by definition (Section 2, page 3).

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should spell out well-filteredness: for every open set U and every filtered family K of nonempty compact saturated subsets of (P, τ), if the intersection of all members of K is contained in U, then some K in K is already contained in U (Section 2, page 3).
The refined question should clarify that this is not the later notion of a Scott well-filtered dcpo, which means specifically that the Scott space ΣP is well-filtered (Definition 4.4, page 6).
The quantifier structure should be explicit: characterize all dcpos P such that there exists at least one topology τ with the above properties.
refined_question: Characterize all directed complete posets P for which there exists a T0 topology τ on the underlying set of P such that cl_τ({x}) = ↓x for every x in P and (P, τ) is well-filtered, i.e. for every open set U in τ and every filtered family K of nonempty compact saturated subsets of (P, τ), if the intersection of all members of K is contained in U, then some K in K is contained in U.
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 4 rather than any earlier introductory conjecture: the paper first defines a well-filtered poset in Definition 4.1, then notes that every well-filtered poset is a dcpo, gives Johnstone's dcpo as a non-example in Example 4.2, and immediately poses Question 4.3: "Characterize the well-filtered dcpos." The draft's phrase "admit some well-filtered topology compatible with their original order" is essentially the content of Definition 4.1, so the nearest official formulation is exactly Question 4.3. The only sharpening needed is to make the compatibility condition explicit and to distinguish this notion from the separate Scott-space notion introduced later in Definition 4.4.
